text: Every FBDI load, no matter the module, follows the exact same sequence of steps. Learn it once, and you can load almost anything. This lesson walks that pipeline start to finish.

Download the template Oracle publishes for your business object. Populate its data tabs with your rows. Generate CSV files using the macro button on the Instructions tab. Zip those CSV files into a single file. Upload that zip to Oracle's content repository, UCM, using File Import and Export.

From there, run Load Interface File for Import — it reads your zip out of UCM and loads it into an interface table, a staging area. Nothing live has changed yet. Then run the product-specific import process, like Import Payables Invoices or Import Journals — it validates each staged row and creates the real record for every row that passes. Finally, review the logs and reports to see what succeeded and what didn't.

Here's the key boundary. Everything up through loading the interface table is just staging — a zip file in UCM, or rows sitting in an interface table, have zero effect on your real ledger or supplier list. Only the second scheduled process, the product-specific import, actually creates real records. That's why you can safely re-run the staging steps as many times as you need while troubleshooting.

Two separate submissions do two separate jobs: Load Interface File for Import stages the data, and the product-specific import process actually creates it. Confusing those two is one of the most common beginner mistakes, and you'll learn to spot it in Chapter 5. Up next, lesson four: a closer look at UCM, the repository every FBDI file passes through.
